In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
X ray tomography is more reliable than FIB tomography for the calculation of the material fractions.
both methods have their own advantages and disadvantages.

FIB SEM tomograpy is superior in terms of resolution and the determination of material fractions, while X ray tomography is superior in terms for the determination of porosity and surface area and the visualization of large sample volumes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the X ray tomography is more suitable for a quantitative analysis of the electrode structure, while the FIB SEM tomograph is better suited for a more qualitative investigation of the electrode microstructure.

the X ray tomography method is more suitable for the determination of the porosity and surface area, whereas the FIB SEM tomographic method is more suitable to distinguish between the different active materials in the blend electrode.
the FIB SEM tomographic results of the LiNiCoAl 2O4 phase are more reliable than the X ray results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3D characterization of battery materials with FIB SEM tomographic methods has a higher potential for a reliable differentiation between the different material phases than X ray tomography.
FIB SEM tomograpy provides the highest quality data for the 3D analysis of Li ion battery cathodes.
both 3D characterization methods can be used to study the complex morphology of Li ion battery electrodes, but the data quality depends on the sample preparation and on the used equipment.
